messages:
maya: Quick proposal — instead of making every client decide what to redact, what if we forward a compact consent token + route hint to the telemetry pipeline and apply redaction/sampling server-side?

sam: curious — how is that different from current per-route sampling?

maya: two diffs: 1) we carry tenant-level consent (opt-in/opt-out + granularity bitmask) so scrubbing rules are deterministic per-tenant; 2) we do stratified sampling post-redaction so billing/metrics aren't biased by dropped PII.

ben: stratified sampling post-redaction sounds good. main concern: perf and storage of full payload before scrub. do we buffer raw text anywhere?

maya: no raw-at-rest. plan is ephemeral in-memory pipeline stage with a strict TTL (5s) — scrub -> compute signatures/metrics -> drop raw. nothing persisted unredacted.

priya: love the TTL constraint. we need an explicit audit path for debug access though — operators sometimes need to inspect a full request for regressions. can we emit a sealed debug blob to a different, tightly RBACed store when tenant allows?

leo: +1 for sealed debug blobs. maybe gate with a per-tenant debug flag and an 'inspect_lease' that auto-expires. ops workflow: request -> legal approval -> short lease.

sam: UX question for console: how do customers see what we scrubbed vs what we dropped? we should avoid surprising them.

maya: console idea: add a 'redaction diff' panel in the request inspector showing anonymized snippets and a list of scrub rules applied. default to summarized view; expand for detail with audit logs only for authorized users.

ben: telemetry-wise we should add two metrics: redaction_false_negative_count and redaction_applied_count per-route. then we can alert on rising FN rate.

devops-bot: deploy-check: redaction_false_negative_count must be emitted at the scrub stage and tagged with sample_reason.

priya: about sampling: if we post-redaction sample, billing and quota enforcement still need stable keys. use a canonical request fingerprint computed after scrub (e.g., hashed route + tenant + prompt-length-bucket) so quota decisions remain consistent.

leo: implementation nit: add header X-RW-Consent: <b64-token> and X-RW-Debug-Lease: <uuid> for debugging; pipeline should validate token via KMS.

sam: I'm worried about header spoofing for ingress customers that don't go through our proxy. we must require auth on any header that affects redaction decisions.

maya: yep — only accept consent header when connection is authenticated (api key or mTLS). otherwise treat as absent. we'll enforce at edge.

ben: for rollout plan: start with dry-run mode for redaction logic (emit diffs + metrics but don't alter stored telemetry), run against 2% traffic for 2 weeks, then increase. Console should show a rollout toggle and the redaction FN heatmap.

priya: need an e2e test matrix: (1) tenant opt-out, (2) tenant partial opt-in, (3) debug-lease flow, (4) header spoof attempt. owners?

sam: I'll pick up tests 1&4. ben take 2, priya take 3?

ben: works for me.

maya: thanks — I'll draft a short RFC and a console mock for the redaction diff panel. pinging @leo for KMS token design.

leo: on it. I'll sketch token format and verification steps by EOD.

priya: one more ask: add a Console metric for "redaction_time_p50/p95" so we can keep tabs on latency impact.

maya: agreed. we'll aim for <3ms p95 extra latency in the scrub stage or automatic fallback to client-side redact if exceeded.

sam: ok — timeline? RFC this week, canary next sprint?

maya: RFC today, infra PR early next week, canary in 2 weeks.

devops-bot: note: created ticket RW-PLT-1123 to track dry-run canary and alerts.

maya: thanks everyone — leaving this thread open for follow-ups.
